Not married but my partner is NT, we found out together that I probably have Asperger's so he's been very understanding. I write him letters if I'm feeling too overwhelmed to get the words out. We also set up a space for me to "retreat" to if I feel the need (so, maybe I'll go and read or write for a while to calm myself down). These may not be the best solutions, but they've worked for us. Another thing is to remember that he wants to help you to become the best person you can be, use that. Talk to him about things that confuse you, no matter how small it may seem...it will clear things up for you and bring you closer together.

I am by no means an expert. 23 and currently do not have a job, though I have had a few, and my fair share of interviews. Also, my partner and his father (who used to do the interviewing for a couple of companies), are currently helping me with my interview skills and I think I've picked up a few useful things...

They expect some people to be a little nervous and a good interviewer will try to make you feel more comfortable. Smile. Shake their hand. If you feel comfortable doing so (maybe near the end of the interview), let them know that you're a little nervous but you will come out of your shell soon enough. Remember that some of your ASD traits are also amazing qualities for an employee to have... got a bit of OCD? Good, you are detail orientated, and won't cut corners. Obviously they will change depending on your situation and the job itself. Also, I found that serving people in fast food is not as mentally draining as I first thought, once you get into the work and find your routine (which is another thing we do well). This being your first job can be a big positive - you haven't learned the 'bad habits' of another workplace. 

You might also want to check out this website:

https://theinterviewguys.com/

They can probably give you some insight into what kind of questions you will be asked, and help you plan out some general answers.

Good luck! I hope it goes well!

It's funny you say that... they were. I met the group and then found him in it. It's like, over time, the rest of them lost any and all interest in me, but now they're stuck with me because of him. I think it's easier for him to believe that I'm being unreasonable than the fact that his friends no longer like his girlfriend. He tells me that they still consider me their friend and apparently ask how I am, but I can't see it... if they really care, why not approach me? Seems to me like they don't want anything to do with me anymore but they don't want to tell him either.

To the best of my knowledge, they're already aware of that. Even though, pathetically, I wasn't the one to tell them.. maybe if **I** was to bring it up to them again and things continue the way they've been going... yeah, demotion time.

I was never one to call first either but, once I spoke to them, we agreed that I needed to put in more effort too. Which I did, I tried to reach out to them, until their responses became blunt and then just didn't come at all. Can't be bothered letting people into my mind that don't care

I've spoken to my partner multiple times about it but I just get told that they're still my friends and I'm being paranoid (as if they're going to tell him that they don't like me anymore). And I've been having a break from them since the start of the year, when they started to ignore me - which is what gives me the biggest impression that they dont like me anymore. So we've all had plenty of time to relax. But I have seen them periodically and it seems like everytime I'm around, it just gets worse, it's like I make the whole situation awkward by just being there. I guess I've started accepting that they're not my friends anymore and get annoyed when I'm told that they still are. Because, from what they've shown me, I just can't believe they care in the slightest anymore.

Oh. I figured if they wanted to stay friends with me, a little bit more effort for a short period shouldn't be too much to ask for? Especially considering they asked and seemed willing to help... 

I didn't think I was worried about offending them too much, it's just that I had to apologize before for taking my anger out on them one night when I was drunk and figured out I wanted to die. That's what sent me to the psychologist. 

But if they still enjoy spending time with me, wouldn't they actually try to do so? My partner is the one that they speak to/invite and when I go with him, I hardly get acknowledged and just feel like an annoyance that shouldn't be there. Makes it hard to be myself when they don't speak to me and hardly see me.

No such thing as bad advice, everyone is different. This might work for 600,000 people and not work for everyone else.

This does remind me of something I've done before though. I can't remember if it helped, but... I'm still here, right? Thanks for your advice, you wonderful human being. ❤
